item.content:encoded:
Our last newsletter was in June, and after a long summer hiatus it’s good to welcome readers back with a renewed sense of energy and hope.

My optimism comes from the collective strategising and illuminating conversations I’ve had with many of you throughout the year.

A central theme which emerged from them is the urgent need to take a longer view of the challenges Europe’s democracies face; to not be totally consumed by our daily struggles.

This is easier said than done in times of deepening division, shrinking civic space, digital disruption, geopolitical tension and war, and as swathes of our electorates abandon faith in democratic institutions.

Yet while the threats we face are immediate and pressing, we will not be able to create healthier, more robust democracies if all we do is respond to them. We must also extend our horizons, challenge ourselves and our approaches, and imagine how the future can be different.

This is the thinking which underpins our foresight initiative #DemocracyFutures.

A compelling story

A central tenet of this initiative is that democracy needs to be able to tell a compelling story. To do so, it must reflect peoples’ hopes and aspirations, connect with their everyday realities, and give them credible reasons to embrace it.

Maria Guerra Arias, our Impact & Learning Manager, expands on these themes in this month’s feature article.

#DemocracyFutures was borne out of a collective process, and the insights of civil society, independent media, philanthropy, and others on the frontlines of protecting democracy across Europe. We are therefore asking the Civitates’ community to engage with the initiative, to challenge our orthodoxies and assumptions, and contribute your perspectives – which will shape our direction of travel.

Europe’s democratic future is still to be determined. Together we can help shape it.

In solidarity,

ELISA PETER

Director, Civitates

 

Across Europe, trust in democracy is faltering, while civil society and independent media are under growing pressure to respond to one crisis after another. But is defending the democratic systems we have enough? What would it take to build a democracy that speaks more convincingly to people’s lives, hopes and aspirations?

In our latest article, Maria Guerra Arias, Civitates’ Impact & Learning Manager, reflects on insights from the first Civitates Forum and introduces #DemocracyFutures – a new initiative asking how today’s choices can shape tomorrow’s democracy. Arguing that Europe’s democratic future is not yet written, Maria asks how democratic actors can move beyond reacting to immediate threats, embrace new ideas and alliances, and offer people a vision of democracy they can believe in.

Read the full article here.

Civitates Forum Report
What happens when you bring together a unique community with first-hand experience of defending democracy to collectively imagine how to work better together, and imagine what the future holds?

Our report captures the insights, challenges and emerging strategies from the first-ever Civitates Forum.Read more here.

 

Reimagining the internet as a public space
The public appetite for loosening big tech’s huge sway over our lives is growing. Dutch coalition PublicSpaces is showing how it can be done.Download and read our annual report here.

Hungarian civil society navigates new political reality
Civil society is continuing to play a crucial role in Hungary’s re-democratisation. Throughout October, the Civil College Foundation (CKA) is organising ‘a month of participation’ offering local communities practical tools to have a say in decisions affecting them. CKA will help local groups organise their own events, as well as create opportunities to present initiatives at their nationally visible programmes. This follows the practical online workshops that CKA hosted in mid-September. Registration and details here.

 

Petition starters boost their media skills
Austrian campaigning CSO #aufstehn recently hosted an online media training for petition starters. It explored how working with the media can support campaigns, and included tips on how to approach journalists, and the benefits and limits of engaging with the media.

 

French Trusted Flaggers: ‘Strengthen our status for us to be effective’
Under the Digital Services Act (DSA), Trusted Flaggers detect illegal content online and notify platforms. Now seven of the nine organisations awarded trusted flagger status by ARCOM, the French regulatory authority, have proposed ways to strengthen their status. The organisations, including Civitates’ partner Point de Contact, made specific calls to the European Commission and ARCOM, including for harmonised procedures, and creating a dedicated European fund for trusted flaggers, to ensure their work is sustainable and independent.

 

Fembloc launches digital gender-based violence training courses
Fembloc, the Catalonia-based a feminist project supporting gender-based violence victims, has launched the second edition of its training courses on digital gender-based violence, aimed at professionals working in violence prevention and response services. They also contributed to a recent discussion on algorithmic justice, focusing on the rights of people affected by automated decision-making systems.

 

Pod črto publish new investigations; launch new podcast season
To mark its 12th anniversary, and as part of its annual #SupportPodCrto campaign, Slovenian independent investigative media outlet Pod črto is publishing a new investigative series which they’ve been working on throughout 2026 (on access to healthcare, intimate violence and road safety). They are also launching a new podcast series, available here.

 

“Freedom of information: six months to avoid sinking”
On September 29 Fonds pour une Presse Libre (FPL), the French coalition supporting press pluralism and independent journalism, held a public meeting to help chart a course for reclaiming the right to speak and to know: “The issue of information—its quality, diversity, independence, and the impartiality of public service broadcasting—is central to this presidential campaign,” they said.

 

“Towards a Society of the Commons”
Wikimedia Europe has co-authored a White Paper with its member Wikimedia France, setting out 28 recommendations to safeguard open, democratically governed digital infrastructure against the risks of generative AI and platform concentration. It was launched this summer in Paris, before an audience of elected officials, government representatives, community members, and representatives of the Wikimedia Foundation and UNESCO.

 

Media partners gather in Gdansk to strengthen resilience

Civitates and Reference Circle, the circle of European independent media, brought together grantees and members respectively for an enlightening gathering on September 24 in Gdansk.

Eszter Szücs and Maria Guerra Arias joined 38 participants exploring organisational resilience (where participants discussed governance arrangements, sustainable leadership and team welfare), financial resilience (participants shared details of their funding challenges and how to overcome them), and on developing AI guidelines for newsrooms.

The majority of participants then went on to the first Breakwater Festival, attended by journalists from Poland, the Nordics and Central and Eastern Europe.

 

Civitates’ team take stock

The Civitates team met in person in Berlin for their annual strategy meeting. It was a moment to take stock of Europe’s shifting democratic landscape, with key elections in many member states coming up, as well as an opportunity to define Civitates’ 2027 workplan, and examine how to best deploy resources.

Civitates also welcomed back from maternity leave Monika Ramos as Programme and Grant officer and Elea Cogoluenhes to the her new job as Engagement and Communications Officer.

Elea will continue to develop the connective tissue between our grantees and foundation partners, sharpening our communications, and helping Civitates grow as a learning platform for democracy across Europe.

 

A new narrative for democracy

On September 21 Civitates co-hosted a webinar with Busara and Liberties on narrative change around democracy. The Democracy Narratives Alliance report argues that this change requires coordination and shared infrastructure across organisations and funders.

Anti-democratic forces are highly effective at coordinating networks and spreading shared narratives, while pro-democracy actors have struggled to do so. One way to rectify this is for advocacy NGOs to communicate the concrete benefits and services they provide, as the public support for NGOs delivering tangible services is clear.

 

7, 14, 21 & 28/10/26 – La Uni Climática (The Climate University)
Location: Online

Climática hosts the seventh edition of its live online Climate University on every Wednesday through October. Under the theme, Against Eco-Anxiety: A Practical Guide to the Eco-Social Transition, the event will feature four masterclasses, six workshops, and a cultural dialogue. Participants include Yayo Herrero, Lucía Martínez (‘Tell Me What You Eat’), Javier Fesser, and many more. Language: Spanish. Register here.

Also available as an on-demand recording.

14/10/26 – Civil Society Co-designing Quality: Building Resilience in a Challenging Environment
Location: KBR – Royal Library of Belgium, Kunstberg/Mont des Arts 28, B-1000 Brussel/Bruxelles.

Civil Society Europe and the CoQuality Network bring together CSOs from across Europe for a conference on building resilience in the third sector. It will build on the findings of an EU level study conducted by the CoQuality network, as well as evidence from practices across Europe. Register here. Draft agenda here.

Week of 19/10/26 – Public Launch | Civitates Future of Democracy in Europe Report
Location: Online

Over the past year Civitates asked civil society leaders, journalists, digital rights experts and funders across Europe what comes next for democracy: what is worth defending, what needs rethinking, and what the field expects of those who fund it. Our new report brings those conversations together. Join us to hear more about why we need a vision for democracy that speaks to people and what it means for civil society, philanthropy and policy-makers. Register here.

 

Calls:

    • Open calls in the Culture Helps Solidarity programme. The European Culture Foundation’s Culture Helps Solidarity project is co-funded by the European Union, and runs from October 2025 until March 2028. It empowers Ukrainian arts and cultural professionals both in Ukraine and the diaspora to sustain creativity, resilience, and community connections during and after the war. The programme currently has an open Collaboration Grant call. The deadline is November 10 and more information is here. The deadline for the Project Grant call is October 6, more information is here.
    • ICNL call for proposals: Defending Digital Rights and Civic Space Online. The International Centre for Not-for-Profit Law (ICNL) is offering grants of up to $23,000 (USD) to support organisations working to protect fundamental freedoms in the digital realm. They’re seeking proposals focused on issues including AI governance, surveillance and privacy, data protection, freedom of expression, and access and inclusion online. Among other areas. Deadline: October 9, 2026. Details are here.

 

Jobs & Opportunities:

    • Head of Philanthropy at Limelight Foundation. Limelight Foundation, a Civitates funding partner and one of Europe’s leading journalism funds, is hiring a Head of Philanthropy to grow its funder network as it sets out to mobilise €150 million for independent journalism over the next decade. Amsterdam-based (hybrid). Apply by 11 October. Details here.
    • Volunteers wanted to fight cyberviolence in France. Point de Contact is seeking volunteers to train so that they can heighten awareness of the huge harm that the growth in cyberviolence (harassment, child sexual abuse material, hate speech, scams, and more) is causing. These volunteers will help spread Point de Contact’s message, and champion its work to a wider audience. Details here.

 

We Recommend:

    • From Pressure to Purpose: A Pathway for the Democracy, Rights, and Governance Community. The Carter Centre’s report, released in July, makes a clarion call for a shift in approach from those working in democracy, human rights, and governance. Using fresh case studies and research it argues that navigating this moment requires shifting weight toward civil society resilience, redistributing power and resources away from centralised and compliance-heavy models, while anchoring democratic legitimacy in lived experience.
    • Defending Human Rights Defenders. Guidance and best practices for National Human Rights Institutions. ENNHRI, the European Network of National Human Rights Institutions, has launched its updated resource on Human Rights Defenders (HRDs). The resource is a living tool for National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs) and others, which outlines the diverse ways that NHRIs promote, protect and support other rights defenders, as well as relevant international and regional standards.
    • Civic Space Tracker. Democracy depends on a vibrant civic space. But across the EU, the freedoms that allow people and organisations to speak out, organise and hold power to account are under increasing pressure. That’s why Liberties has launched a new Civic Space Tracker, a unique tool for monitoring legal threats to civic space across the European Union.
    • Resisting restrictive laws: A practical guide for democracy defenders. In recent years there’s been a global trend for countries to adopt laws restricting the work of civil society organisations (CSOs), social movements and independent media, endangering fundamental freedom. This detailed new guide by the European Centre for Not-for-Profit Law (ENCL) offers a practical guide for navigating these challenges.
    • Trends in the Information Environment: 2026 Expert Survey Results. The International Panel on the Information Environment’s (IPIE’s) fourth annual expert survey included 470 experts studying the information environment across 71 countries. Among other findings the report shows that pessimism is at its highest level yet, while the experts agree that a healthy information environment most needs accurate information and a diversity of voices.

ARTICLE 19, which defends freedom of expression and access to information across Europe and Central Asia, has just launched a new report exploring digital transnational repression against civil society in exile, specifically those operating in a Belarusian and Russian language environment.

item.title: Utdeling av Free Media Awards for 2026
item.description:
Årets vinnere av Free Media Awards fra Stiftelsen Fritt Ord og Zeit Stiftung Bucerius tok imot prisene i Toppsalen på Munch-museet i Oslo 29. september 2026.
Den belarusiske journalisten og medielederen Andrei Aliaksandrau kom direkte til Oslo etter å ha sittet over fem år i fengsel for sitt virke. Han dedikerte prisen til fengslede journalister og redaktører i Belarus og brukte Liverpool-lagets refereng: “You’ll never walk alone”.

Mykhailo Tkach leder gravejournalistikken i Ukrainska Pravda som avdekker korrupsjon, også i et Ukraina som kjemper en eksistensiell krig mot Russland.
– Jeg er siktet i minst tretten saker knyttet til jobben min. Jeg har blitt truet. Teamet mitt har blitt truet. Og hva er svaret vårt? Å fortsette å grave. Å tie beskytter ikke demokratiet. Det gjør journalistikk.

Photos from ceremony / Pressebilder

Se og hør talene her

– Journalistikk er å samle inn fakta, sjekke dem så godt vi kan og skille fakta fra propaganda. Femten av mine kollegaer er fortsatt i fengsel. Jeg tar imot denne prisen på vegne av dem, sa den nylig løslatte medielederen Andrei Aliaksandrau.

Han takket for solidariteten mens han var i fengsel.

– Det er ekstremt viktig. Vi merker denne solidariteten og støtten og den hjelper oss stort.

Forfatter Erika Fatland holdt talen til årets mottakere og nevnte hvordan Aliaksandrau mange ganger bruke fotballlagets Liverpools sang “You´ll never walk alone” for å holde motet opp i fengsel.

Hun sa også at det frie ord har makt, også i diktaturer.

– Autoritære regimer frykter ord. Fra reisene mine i to autoritære regimer har jeg lært én ting: Diktatorer er redde for journalister og forfattere.

Noe av det aller første de gjør, er å bringe den frie pressen til taushet. Fordi de er redde for ord. Fordi ord avslører dem. Og det er nesten rørende, men også svært talende, hvordan tollere i autoritære regimer har en tendens til å behandle bøker som om de var farlig sprengstoff, sa Fatland.

Her ble Fatland støttet av Fritt Ords direktør Knut Olav Åmås og lederen for Zeit Stiftung Bucerius, Manuel J. Hartung.
– Journalistikk taler sannhet til makten, speaks truth to power, sa Åmås i velkomsthilsenen sin, men minnet også om at forholdene for pressefrihet nå er de dårligste på over 20 år.

Hartung, minnet om hvor mange journalister som hvert år fengsles, drepes eller bortføres på grunn av arbeidet sitt. Den drepte russiske reporteren Anna Politkovskaja har fått en plass oppkalt etter seg i Hamburg.

– Plassen er en daglig påminnelse om hvor viktig pressefrihet er. Vi står sammen med dere, sa Hartung.

Juryens talsperson, journalisten Attila Mong, sa at «Free Media Awards er vår måte å uttrykke respekt og beundring for motet og motstandskraften prisvinnerne viser når de fortsetter arbeidet sitt til tross for trusler og voldelig undertrykkelse».

Alle tre takket mottakerne for arbeidet de gjør for ytringsfrihet hver eneste dag.

Fatland gikk gjennom utviklingen for pressefrihet i mange av landene.

– I Georgia har friheten blitt innskrenket dramatisk på få år. Armenia har falt på pressefrihetsindeksen, selv om det fortsatt er regionens frieste presse. Og Russland er nå helt nede på 172. plass av 180 land i verdens pressefrihetsindeks.

Likevel fortsetter russiske journalister arbeidet fra eksil, sa Fatland og i Ukraina fortsetter journalistikken til tross for krigen.

– Sannhet er krigens første offer, men heller aldri så viktig som under krig, minnet Fatland om og siterte Mykhailo Tkach som sa “Å tie ikke beskytter ikke demokratiet. Det gjør journalistikk”.

– Ukrainske journalister jobber under beskytning, selv når de er langt unna frontlinjene, sa Tkach.
– I et land som kjemper for sin frihet, er ikke en fri presse en luksus. Den er en del av det vi kjemper for – og en del av det som holder demokratiet vårt i live.

Presset mot den kritiske presse vedvarer – ikke bare mot Ukrainska Pravda, men også mot de få andre uavhengige mediene som er igjen i Ukraina. Erfaringen har likevel lært oss at det å stille ubehagelige spørsmål, avdekke sannheten og holde makthavere ansvarlige kan redde liv, sa han.

Nino Bakradze, sjefredaktør i det undersøkende mediet iFact har tidligere kritisert “Loven om utenlandske agenter i Georgia”.

– Georgias store problen er at det å blitt straffbart å fortelle sannheten. Likevel fortsetter vi. Lyset må holdes tent. Uavhengig journalistikk betyr noe. Fri presse betyr noe. Arbeidet vi gjør hver dag, kan forandre ting til det bedre, sa Bakradze.

Arevhat Sahakyan, journalist og direktør i online-mediet Factor TV fra Armenia sa at journalistikk handler om å holde makthaverne ansvarlige.

Lola Tagaeva, sjefredaktør i det russiske online-mediet Verstka, som opererer fra eksil, sa at “å støtte undersøkende journalistikk handler om å bevare frihet”.

– Vi er et av de mest siterte russiske eksilmediene og gjennom deling treffer mange flere enn bare våre egne lesere med informasjonen vi avdekker.

Nettsiden vår er blokkert i Russland, men vi vet vi når millioner, sa Tagaeva.

Aliaksandrau fra Belarus holdt siste tale under utdelingen og han avrundet poenget sitt og budskapet med nettopp de ordene som hadde holdt motet hans oppe gjennom de mange årene i fengsel:

“You´ll never walk alone”.

Duoen Rohey Taalah & Martin Myhre Olsen stod for musikkinnslag med låtene Diamonds (Laura Myula), Both Sides Now (Joni Mitchell) og Bright Sunny South (trad.)

Her kan du lese om forrige utdeling av Free Media Awards i Oslo i 2024 og i utdelingen i 2022, da fullskala-invasjonen av Ukraina var i sitt første år.

Om Free Media Awards
Free Media Awards er presseprisene som tildeles av de to stiftelsene Fritt Ord, Oslo, og Zeit Stiftung Bucerius, Hamburg. Presseprisene søker å rette oppmerksomheten mot og styrke den uavhengige rollen til journalister og medier i Øst- og Sentral-Europa.

Mykhailo Tkach (Ukraina)
Mykhailo Tkach får en Free Media Award for sin fryktløse og konsistente undersøkende journalistikk i krigstid. Som leder for gravejournalistikken i Ukrainska Pravda, har hans arbeid bidratt til å forme den offentlige debatten i Ukraina og internasjonalt gjennom å avdekke korrupsjonssaker og maktmisbruk. Hans avsløringer av korrupsjon i forbindelse med inngåelse av statlige kontrakter og leveranser til forsvaret, eller av privilegert behandling av rike mennesker og luksuslivet til enkelte i den ukrainske eliten i utlandet etter den russiske invasjonen spiller en viktig rolle for samfunnet. Hans nylige rapportering om utviklingen knyttet til Operasjon Midas er et eksempel på journalistikk som sørger for at saker av stor offentlig interesse blir gjenstand for gransking. Tkach har også etterforsket og avslørt skjult russisk påvirkning i vestlige land. Han har vært utsatt for trusler en rekke ganger. Tkachs rapportering er et glimrende eksempel på at undersøkende journalistikk er mulig og helt avgjørende for et land i krig. I 2026 mottok Tkach Georgiy Gongadze Prize, en av Ukrainas mest anerkjente utmerkelser for uavhengig journalistikk.

iFact (Georgia)
iFact får en Free Media Award for deres betydningsfulle undersøkende journalistikk om saker av stor offentlig interesse i Georgia som andre forsøker å skjule. Gravejournalistene i det Tbilisi-baserte mediet står bak større undersøkelser om russisk innflytelse i landet og dens bånd til partiet Georgisk Drøm så vel som om korrupsjon i eliten på statlig nivå. Noen av iFacts rapporter som har fått størst gjennomslag i offentligheten, handler om undergravingen av uavhengigheten til sivilombudet i landet, om å misbruke grensene i Georgia som «grønne korridorer» for å unngå sanksjoner og om russisk finansiering av georgiske organisasjoner for å fremme pro-russiske meninger. iFact har med stor integritet bidratt i journalistiske samarbeid på tvers av grenser. Til tross for økende press fortsetter iFact å være en bunnsolid medieplattform. iFact ble grunnlagt i 2016 av Nino Bakradze og Nino Gagua. Nino Bakradze har hatt stillingen som sjefredaktør helt fra starten av.

Factor TV (Armenia)
Jerevan-baserte Factor TV får en Free Media Award for deres selvstendige og faktabaserte journalistikk som klart bidrar til en mer nyansert offentlig debatt i Armenia. Gjennom grundig rapportering, undersøkelser og analyser skjærer Factor TV gjennom desinformasjon og propaganda, og har etablert seg som en av Armenias ledende uavhengige og troverdige mediekanaler. Mediet har utmerket seg med undersøkende journalistikk og tatt en vaktbikkje-rolle; de har avdekket korrupsjon, interessekonflikter, brudd på integritet og maktmisbruk, noe som har ført til både strafferettslige etterforskninger og disiplinærsaker. Factor TV rapporterer også omfattende om menneskerettigheter, vold mot kvinner, minoritetsrettigheter og andre sensitive eller underbelyste saker. I en tid preget av økende desinformasjon, politisert propaganda, hatefulle ytringer samt utenlandsk informasjonsmanipulasjon og innblanding, avslører Factor TV systematisk villedende narrativer, forebygger og tilbakeviser desinformasjon, og gir publikum verifisert informasjon og kontekst. Factor TV ble grunnlagt i 2017 av Arevhat Sahakyan, leder for organisasjonen Factor Information Center. Vanik Hakobyan er sjefredaktør.

Verstka (Russland)
Det uavhengige online-mediet Verstka ble etablert i april 2022 som en respons på ødeleggelsen av russiske medier under Russlands fullskala invasjon av Ukraina. Verstka, som har base i Praha, får en Free Media Award for å være en troverdig førstehåndskilde til de menneskelige omkostningene ved krigen, militarisering og undertrykkelse, vold i hjemmet og kjønnsbasert vold og forfølgelse av LGBTQ+miljøer. Journalistene dokumenterer ofte erfaringene til de som motsetter seg krigen. Verstka rapporterer om Russland uten å ta hensyn til sensur, press eller manipulasjon. De har blitt ett av de mest siterte uavhengige russiske mediene som dekker politikk, samfunn og kultur. Russland blokkerte Verstka i juni 2022, og sjefredaktør Lola Tagaeva ble utpekt som «utenlandsk agent» i januar 2024. Allikevel fortsetter Vertska å rapportere fra domstolene og regionene ved å bruke kilder som står overfor personlig risiko.

Andrei Aliaksandrau (Belarus)
Journalist og medieleder Andrei Aliaksandrau, som i dag er fengslet i Belarus, får en Free Media Award for sitt mot og sin forpliktelse til presse- og ytringsfrihet under et i økende grad repressivt regime. Gjennom sitt arbeid i det uavhengige belarusiske nyhetsbyrået BelaPAN og Belarusian Association of Journalists (BAJ) har han bidratt til å styrke profesjonelle journalistiske standarder, støtte uavhengige medier og til å bygge opp internasjonale nettverk med journalister og menneskerettighetsforkjempere. Andrei Aliaksandrau ble arrestert for sitt virke i 2021, og i 2022 ble han dømt til 14 års fengsel med fabrikerte anklager. Han er anerkjent for å være en politisk fange.

Hvordan velges vinnerne av Free Media Awards?
Alle kandidatene ble nominert av internasjonale institusjoner og organisasjoner som er aktive i Øst- og Sentral-Europa, så vel som eksperter på regionen. En internasjonal jury har valgt prisvinnerne. Juryen for 2026 består av Alice Bota, Øst-Europa-reporter for Die ZEIT; Juri Durkot, ukrainsk journalist og oversetter; Attila Mong, Berlin-basert representant i Europa for The Committee to Protect Journalist; Inna Sangadzhieva, avdelingssjef for Europa og Sentral-Asia i Den norske Helsingforskomité; og Silvia Stöber, seniorreporter for Correctiv.

Om presseprisene Free Media Awards

Presseprisene Free Media Awards er øremerket journalister og medier i Øst- og Sentral-Europa. Prisen tildeles i samarbeid mellom Stiftelsen Fritt Ord i Norge og Zeit Stiftung Bucerius i Tyskland.

Prisen deles ut annethvert år i Oslo og Hamburg.

Foto i fotogalleriet: Linda Bournane Engelberth. De seks siste er tatt av Krister Sørbø for NRK

– Autoritære regimer frykter ord. Fra reisene mine i to autoritære regimer har jeg lært én ting: Diktatorer er redde for journalister og forfattere.

Noe av det aller første de gjør, er å bringe den frie pressen til taushet. Fordi de er redde for ord. Fordi ord avslører dem. Og det er nesten rørende, men også svært talende, hvordan tollere i autoritære regimer har en tendens til å behandle bøker som om de var farlig sprengstoff, sa Fatland.

Her ble Fatland støttet av Fritt Ords direktør Knut Olav Åmås og lederen for Zeit Stiftung Bucerius, Manuel J. Hartung.
– Journalistikk taler sannhet til makten, speaks truth to power, sa Åmås i velkomsthilsenen sin, men minnet også om at forholdene for pressefrihet nå er de dårligste på over 20 år.

Hartung, minnet om hvor mange journalister som hvert år fengsles, drepes eller bortføres på grunn av arbeidet sitt. Den drepte russiske reporteren Anna Politkovskaja har fått en plass oppkalt etter seg i Hamburg.

– Plassen er en daglig påminnelse om hvor viktig pressefrihet er. Vi står sammen med dere, sa Hartung.

Juryens talsperson, journalisten Attila Mong, sa at «Free Media Awards er vår måte å uttrykke respekt og beundring for motet og motstandskraften prisvinnerne viser når de fortsetter arbeidet sitt til tross for trusler og voldelig undertrykkelse».

Alle tre takket mottakerne for arbeidet de gjør for ytringsfrihet hver eneste dag.

Fatland gikk gjennom utviklingen for pressefrihet i mange av landene.

– I Georgia har friheten blitt innskrenket dramatisk på få år. Armenia har falt på pressefrihetsindeksen, selv om det fortsatt er regionens frieste presse. Og Russland er nå helt nede på 172. plass av 180 land i verdens pressefrihetsindeks.

Likevel fortsetter russiske journalister arbeidet fra eksil, sa Fatland og i Ukraina fortsetter journalistikken til tross for krigen.

– Sannhet er krigens første offer, men heller aldri så viktig som under krig, minnet Fatland om og siterte Mykhailo Tkach som sa “Å tie ikke beskytter ikke demokratiet. Det gjør journalistikk”.

– Ukrainske journalister jobber under beskytning, selv når de er langt unna frontlinjene, sa Tkach.
– I et land som kjemper for sin frihet, er ikke en fri presse en luksus. Den er en del av det vi kjemper for – og en del av det som holder demokratiet vårt i live.

Presset mot den kritiske presse vedvarer – ikke bare mot Ukrainska Pravda, men også mot de få andre uavhengige mediene som er igjen i Ukraina. Erfaringen har likevel lært oss at det å stille ubehagelige spørsmål, avdekke sannheten og holde makthavere ansvarlige kan redde liv, sa han.

Nino Bakradze, sjefredaktør i det undersøkende mediet iFact har tidligere kritisert “Loven om utenlandske agenter i Georgia”.

– Georgias store problen er at det å blitt straffbart å fortelle sannheten. Likevel fortsetter vi. Lyset må holdes tent. Uavhengig journalistikk betyr noe. Fri presse betyr noe. Arbeidet vi gjør hver dag, kan forandre ting til det bedre, sa Bakradze.

Arevhat Sahakyan, journalist og direktør i online-mediet Factor TV fra Armenia sa at journalistikk handler om å holde makthaverne ansvarlige.

Lola Tagaeva, sjefredaktør i det russiske online-mediet Verstka, som opererer fra eksil, sa at “å støtte undersøkende journalistikk handler om å bevare frihet”.

– Vi er et av de mest siterte russiske eksilmediene og gjennom deling treffer mange flere enn bare våre egne lesere med informasjonen vi avdekker.

Nettsiden vår er blokkert i Russland, men vi vet vi når millioner, sa Tagaeva.

Aliaksandrau fra Belarus holdt siste tale under utdelingen og han avrundet poenget sitt og budskapet med nettopp de ordene som hadde holdt motet hans oppe gjennom de mange årene i fengsel:

“You´ll never walk alone”.

Duoen Rohey Taalah & Martin Myhre Olsen stod for musikkinnslag med låtene Diamonds (Laura Myula), Both Sides Now (Joni Mitchell) og Bright Sunny South (trad.)

Her kan du lese om forrige utdeling av Free Media Awards i Oslo i 2024 og i utdelingen i 2022, da fullskala-invasjonen av Ukraina var i sitt første år.

Om Free Media Awards
Free Media Awards er presseprisene som tildeles av de to stiftelsene Fritt Ord, Oslo, og Zeit Stiftung Bucerius, Hamburg. Presseprisene søker å rette oppmerksomheten mot og styrke den uavhengige rollen til journalister og medier i Øst- og Sentral-Europa.

Mykhailo Tkach (Ukraina)
Mykhailo Tkach får en Free Media Award for sin fryktløse og konsistente undersøkende journalistikk i krigstid. Som leder for gravejournalistikken i Ukrainska Pravda, har hans arbeid bidratt til å forme den offentlige debatten i Ukraina og internasjonalt gjennom å avdekke korrupsjonssaker og maktmisbruk. Hans avsløringer av korrupsjon i forbindelse med inngåelse av statlige kontrakter og leveranser til forsvaret, eller av privilegert behandling av rike mennesker og luksuslivet til enkelte i den ukrainske eliten i utlandet etter den russiske invasjonen spiller en viktig rolle for samfunnet. Hans nylige rapportering om utviklingen knyttet til Operasjon Midas er et eksempel på journalistikk som sørger for at saker av stor offentlig interesse blir gjenstand for gransking. Tkach har også etterforsket og avslørt skjult russisk påvirkning i vestlige land. Han har vært utsatt for trusler en rekke ganger. Tkachs rapportering er et glimrende eksempel på at undersøkende journalistikk er mulig og helt avgjørende for et land i krig. I 2026 mottok Tkach Georgiy Gongadze Prize, en av Ukrainas mest anerkjente utmerkelser for uavhengig journalistikk.

iFact (Georgia)
iFact får en Free Media Award for deres betydningsfulle undersøkende journalistikk om saker av stor offentlig interesse i Georgia som andre forsøker å skjule. Gravejournalistene i det Tbilisi-baserte mediet står bak større undersøkelser om russisk innflytelse i landet og dens bånd til partiet Georgisk Drøm så vel som om korrupsjon i eliten på statlig nivå. Noen av iFacts rapporter som har fått størst gjennomslag i offentligheten, handler om undergravingen av uavhengigheten til sivilombudet i landet, om å misbruke grensene i Georgia som «grønne korridorer» for å unngå sanksjoner og om russisk finansiering av georgiske organisasjoner for å fremme pro-russiske meninger. iFact har med stor integritet bidratt i journalistiske samarbeid på tvers av grenser. Til tross for økende press fortsetter iFact å være en bunnsolid medieplattform. iFact ble grunnlagt i 2016 av Nino Bakradze og Nino Gagua. Nino Bakradze har hatt stillingen som sjefredaktør helt fra starten av.

Factor TV (Armenia)
Jerevan-baserte Factor TV får en Free Media Award for deres selvstendige og faktabaserte journalistikk som klart bidrar til en mer nyansert offentlig debatt i Armenia. Gjennom grundig rapportering, undersøkelser og analyser skjærer Factor TV gjennom desinformasjon og propaganda, og har etablert seg som en av Armenias ledende uavhengige og troverdige mediekanaler. Mediet har utmerket seg med undersøkende journalistikk og tatt en vaktbikkje-rolle; de har avdekket korrupsjon, interessekonflikter, brudd på integritet og maktmisbruk, noe som har ført til både strafferettslige etterforskninger og disiplinærsaker. Factor TV rapporterer også omfattende om menneskerettigheter, vold mot kvinner, minoritetsrettigheter og andre sensitive eller underbelyste saker. I en tid preget av økende desinformasjon, politisert propaganda, hatefulle ytringer samt utenlandsk informasjonsmanipulasjon og innblanding, avslører Factor TV systematisk villedende narrativer, forebygger og tilbakeviser desinformasjon, og gir publikum verifisert informasjon og kontekst. Factor TV ble grunnlagt i 2017 av Arevhat Sahakyan, leder for organisasjonen Factor Information Center. Vanik Hakobyan er sjefredaktør.

Verstka (Russland)
Det uavhengige online-mediet Verstka ble etablert i april 2022 som en respons på ødeleggelsen av russiske medier under Russlands fullskala invasjon av Ukraina. Verstka, som har base i Praha, får en Free Media Award for å være en troverdig førstehåndskilde til de menneskelige omkostningene ved krigen, militarisering og undertrykkelse, vold i hjemmet og kjønnsbasert vold og forfølgelse av LGBTQ+miljøer. Journalistene dokumenterer ofte erfaringene til de som motsetter seg krigen. Verstka rapporterer om Russland uten å ta hensyn til sensur, press eller manipulasjon. De har blitt ett av de mest siterte uavhengige russiske mediene som dekker politikk, samfunn og kultur. Russland blokkerte Verstka i juni 2022, og sjefredaktør Lola Tagaeva ble utpekt som «utenlandsk agent» i januar 2024. Allikevel fortsetter Vertska å rapportere fra domstolene og regionene ved å bruke kilder som står overfor personlig risiko.

Andrei Aliaksandrau (Belarus)
Journalist og medieleder Andrei Aliaksandrau, som i dag er fengslet i Belarus, får en Free Media Award for sitt mot og sin forpliktelse til presse- og ytringsfrihet under et i økende grad repressivt regime. Gjennom sitt arbeid i det uavhengige belarusiske nyhetsbyrået BelaPAN og Belarusian Association of Journalists (BAJ) har han bidratt til å styrke profesjonelle journalistiske standarder, støtte uavhengige medier og til å bygge opp internasjonale nettverk med journalister og menneskerettighetsforkjempere. Andrei Aliaksandrau ble arrestert for sitt virke i 2021, og i 2022 ble han dømt til 14 års fengsel med fabrikerte anklager. Han er anerkjent for å være en politisk fange.

Hvordan velges vinnerne av Free Media Awards?
Alle kandidatene ble nominert av internasjonale institusjoner og organisasjoner som er aktive i Øst- og Sentral-Europa, så vel som eksperter på regionen. En internasjonal jury har valgt prisvinnerne. Juryen for 2026 består av Alice Bota, Øst-Europa-reporter for Die ZEIT; Juri Durkot, ukrainsk journalist og oversetter; Attila Mong, Berlin-basert representant i Europa for The Committee to Protect Journalist; Inna Sangadzhieva, avdelingssjef for Europa og Sentral-Asia i Den norske Helsingforskomité; og Silvia Stöber, seniorreporter for Correctiv.

Om presseprisene Free Media Awards

Presseprisene Free Media Awards er øremerket journalister og medier i Øst- og Sentral-Europa. Prisen tildeles i samarbeid mellom Stiftelsen Fritt Ord i Norge og Zeit Stiftung Bucerius i Tyskland.

Prisen deles ut annethvert år i Oslo og Hamburg.

Foto i fotogalleriet: Linda Bournane Engelberth. De seks siste er tatt av Krister Sørbø for NRK

item.title: The Tinius Trust joins international effort on traceable information in the age of AI
item.description:
29. september 2026

The Tinius Trust is joining the venture studio Signals at Scale as a partner. The studio defines the problems to be solved in the emerging AI-mediated information ecosystem and funds those building systems that make the information reaching users through artificial intelligence possible to verify.

Signals at Scale was founded by Shuwei Fang, a Shorenstein Fellow at Harvard Kennedy School, and David Caswell, formerly head of AI innovation at BBC News Labs. Signals at Scale identifies challenges in the emerging ecosystem, assembles small teams around each challenge, funds them and sets deadlines.

The studio starts from the assumption of a greatly expanded information ecosystem, with vastly more information flowing through it. Functions such as traceability, verification and compensation look very different if information output is 100 or 1,000 times what manual workflows produce today, or if consumption becomes dramatically more personalised and relevant.

Why the Tinius Trust is taking part

As a long-term media owner, the Tinius Trust wants to help build this infrastructure for crediting and paying sources.

"The Tinius Trust works to secure good conditions for free media, as our articles of association require. For a long time that has meant legislation and source protection. Now a large part of the framework is set in the technology itself, in how language models choose sources, what they credit and how errors are corrected. No common standard is in place yet, and nobody knows where it will be made. Signals at Scale is one of several attempts. We would rather take part in those attempts than wait for an answer from the technology giants," says Nicklas Stavnar, Head of Foresight at the Tinius Trust.

What the partnership involves

The partnership runs for two years, from 1 September 2026. The Tinius Trust contributes around NOK 3.1 million a year.

Earlier work with the same researchers

This is the second time the Tinius Trust has worked with Caswell and Fang. In 2025 the trust funded and took part in the project AI in Journalism Futures 2025. The project is published here

Flere nyheter

28. mai 2026

Adele Matheson Mestad joins the board of the Tinius Trust

Adele Matheson Mestad. former Director of the Norwegian National Human Rights Institution, now partner at BAHR, is a new member of the Board at the Tinius Trust. "With Adele Matheson Mestad, we gain solid knowledge of human rights, freedom of expression and technological development, and above all, a wise mind with fresh perspectives," says Board Chair Ole Jacob Sunde.

28. mai 2026

Raoul Grünthal new Chair of the Tinius Trust

Raoul Grünthal has been elected as the new Chair of the Tinius Trust, effective 17 June. "I really look forward to leading this board in an incredibly exciting time," he says.

15. oktober 2025

New report: the future of media as seen by 1000 AI personas

The Tinius Trust launches AI in Journalism Futures 2025 - a groundbreaking experiment in which artificial intelligence has replicated a large-scale scenario planning project about the future of journalism. Read more here.

26. mars 2025

Court gives green light to Norwegian state mass surveillance

Today, the Oslo District Court fully supported the Norwegian state in the case regarding the Norwegian Intelligence Service's mass surveillance, brought by the Tinius Trust and editor Tom Erik Thorsen.

item.title: Sep 28 Mo, 28. Sep 2026 19:00 Uhr Globales Kräftemessen: Russland und Europa Gespräch • KörberForum
item.description:
• KörberForum
  • Europa stärken
  • Gespräch
  • Europa
  • Internationale Politik
  • Politik
  • Russland

Russland ist im Westen isoliert – nicht jedoch in der Welt. Moskau schmiedet nicht erst seit 2022 Allianzen, umwirbt den Globalen Süden und untergräbt den westlichen Einfluss. Wie erfolgreich diese Strategie ist und welche Antwort Europa findet, besprechen wir mit der Russlandexpertin Hanna Notte und dem Europapolitiker Sergey Lagodinsky.

Aus westlicher Perspektive gilt Russland seit dem Angriff auf die Ukraine 2022 als international isoliert. Umfassende Sanktionen und die weitgehende wirtschaftliche Entkopplung haben das Verhältnis zwischen dem Kreml und Europa tiefgreifend verändert und sind Ausdruck einer neuen Phase geopolitischer Spannungen.

Der Blick über Europa und Nordamerika hinaus zeigt jedoch ein komplexeres Bild: In zahlreichen Regionen der Welt bleibt Russland ein relevanter und einflussreicher politischer, wirtschaftlicher und sicherheitspolitischer Akteur.

Über Energieexporte, Waffenlieferungen und die diplomatische Zusammenarbeit in Formaten wie den BRICS-Staaten verfolgt Russland seit Jahren eine Strategie, die auf den Ausbau seines globalen Handlungsspielraums und die Begrenzung westlicher Einflusszonen abzielt.

Dabei inszeniert sich Moskau international als Gegenpol zu den USA und Europa und bekräftigt bestehende Kritik an internationalen Macht- und Abhängigkeitsverhältnissen an.

Handelt es sich hierbei um eine nachhaltige geopolitische Neuordnung oder um Zweckbündnisse mit begrenzter Reichweite? Wer trägt russische Interessen jenseits des Kremls in die Welt? Und welche Antworten findet Europa auf diese Strategie?

Diese Fragen diskutiert Leslie Schübel, Körber-Stiftung, mit dem Europaabgeordneten Sergey Lagodinsky und die Russlandexpertin Hanna Notte. 

Gäste

  • Sergey Lagodinsky ist promovierter Jurist, Autor und Mitglied des Europäischen Parlaments (Bündnis 90/Die Grünen), sowie stellvertretender Fraktionsvorsitzender der Greens/EFA-Fraktion. Er ist Mitglied des Rechtsausschusses sowie im Ausschuss für Auswärtige Angelegenheiten. Außerdem ist er rechtspolitischer Sprecher der Greens/EFA Fraktion sowie Sprecher für Russland und Transatlantische Beziehungen der Greens/EFA Fraktion.

  • Hanna Notte leitet das Eurasien-Programm des James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies und ist Senior Associate am CSIS in Washington. Notte ist promovierte Politikwissenschaftlerin und studierte an den Universitäten Cambridge und Oxford. Sie schreibt regelmäßig für die Financial Times, New York Times und Zeit. Ihr Buch „We Shall Outlast Them: Putin’s Global Campaign To Defeat the West" erschien 2026.

Moderation

  • Leslie Schübel ist Programmleiterin Internationale Politik für das Berliner Forum Außenpolitik und das Körber Policy Game bei der Körber-Stiftung in Berlin. In der Vergangenheit hat sie für das EU Russia Expert Network on Foreign Policy gearbeitet. Inhaltlich beschäftigt Sie sich mit russischer Innen- und Außenpolitik sowie mit den Ländern der Östlichen Partnerschaft. Leslie Schübel hat Masterabschlüsse in Internationalen Beziehungen von der Freien Universität Berlin und dem Moskauer Institut für Internationale Beziehungen (MGIMO).

Veranstaltungsort und Anfahrt

20457 Hamburg

item.title: Read more about DRC: Ebola is also an information crisis
item.description:
When an Ebola outbreak hits a community, people need reliable information to understand the disease, assess risks and decide where to find care. For journalists, providing this information requires more than reporting the latest case numbers. In eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, misinformation and distrust are creating an additional challenge.

A recent rapid needs assessment by ActionAid DRC across three health zones in Ituri found that only 64% of respondents believed Ebola was a real disease and not linked to spiritual or mystical causes. Only 34% could correctly identify at least three ways Ebola is transmitted. This means journalists are reporting in an environment where basic questions about the disease itself are still contested.

Raoul Kamanda, Director of PNCPS at the Ministry of Health in the DRC, stresses that the way information is communicated matters. He describes how information can either deepen mistrust or help build confidence in the response:“A lot of information can inflame a situation, distort understanding and destroy trust. Other information can build trust and buy-in.”

A long-standing information problem

This is not a new challenge in the DRC. During the 2018-2019 Ebola outbreak in North Kivu, a population-based study found that 92% of respondents had heard at least one common misinformation claim about Ebola. Almost half, 46%, believed at least one of these claims. One in four believed the statement that Ebola did not exist.

Recent monitoring indicates that misinformation remains a big problem during the current outbreak. WHO's Africa Infodemic Response Alliance has documented rumours about safe burial practices and treatment, traditional remedies and the financing of the Ebola response. Raoul Kamanda, Director of the National Program for Communication and Health Promotion (PNCPS) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and one of the speakers in our upcoming webinar series for journalists covering the outbreak, also points to the role of traditional and religious figures in spreading false information:"There are also traditional healers or pastors who give false testimonies, false prophecies."

These rumours come from genuine questions and concerns. According to the Centre for Information Resilience (CIR), communities in eastern DRC have experienced 17 Ebola outbreaks since 1976, alongside decades of conflict, displacement and resource extraction. The CIR recently examined how this history shapes the current sceptic reponse. Their research points to previous scandals and alleged abuses linked to international aid organisations, as well as low trust in health authorities and international actors. These experiences have created a deep mistrust around Ebola and the people responding to it giving misinformation more room to spread.

These rumours are a real problem for journalists as well. Congolese journalist Tuver Wundi has seen how mis- and disinformation can affect both journalists and the communities they work in: “Yes, there were quite a few [rumours], because people believed journalists were moving around [spreading the disease], Wundi says. “In Nyania, for example, there were protests against the response and journalists were targeted.”

The role of journalists

This makes the work of local journalists especially important. Journalists have to answer difficult questions, verify and debunk competing claims in a context where misinformation is widespread. What exactly is the virus? How does it spread? What information about vaccines and treatment is reliable? How should journalists report on deaths, survivors and burials? And what should they do when a dangerous rumour starts circulating in their community? To answer these journalists need information from reliable sources and specialist knowledge. They also need to protect themselves. Journalists in affected areas also risk their own health.

Reporting on Ebola also requires journalists to understand the medical realities behind the outbreak. Popaul Nunza, Head of Communication at the National Institute for Biomedical Research in the DRC, says the absence of specific treatment for the current strain has created understandable fear.“We had neither therapy nor specific medication for this strain. When you announce a strain with no specific medication, it's frightening. That fear is understandable.” [..]. People are also skeptical. “People kept asking: ‘Why go to the hospital if there's no medicine for this strain?’”, Nunza says.

Supporting journalists on the ground

Free Press Unlimited is supporting journalists covering the Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC through a series of three practical webinars. The webinars bring together Congolese health experts, government officials and experienced journalists to address the questions journalists face when reporting on the outbreak.

The three sessions focus on:

  • Understanding the disease
  • Staying safe as a journalist in an affected area
  • Reporting accurately and ethically

The discussions will cover both the medical and journalistic challenges of reporting on Ebola. This includes understanding how the virus spreads, identifying reliable information about treatment and vaccines, staying safe while reporting from affected areas, and dealing with rumours and misinformation.

More information about the webinars (in French)

Following the webinars, Free Press Unlimited will publish a series of practical training manuals covering the same three topics. The manuals are being developed together with Congolese infectious disease and public health experts, senior Ministry of Health officials and journalists covering the outbreak. The manuals will be available in French, Swahili and Lingala, giving journalists access to the information and practical guidance beyond the live sessions.

Reliable information matters

During an Ebola outbreak, journalists need access to reliable information and practical guidance to report accurately and responsibly. By bringing together experts and journalists through the webinars and making the knowledge available through practical training manuals, Free Press Unlimited is supporting journalists who are reporting on the outbreak in eastern DRC.

item.title: Read more about CPJ review confirms: Israel still responsible for majority of killings of journalists and media workers worldwide since 2023
item.description:
The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has documented the killing of journalists and media workers in Israel and the occupied Palestinian territory since October 7, 2023. In June 2026, CPJ announced a comprehensive review of its database after Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad published obituaries identifying as combatants a number of individuals whom CPJ had documented as journalists or media workers. 

Free Press Unlimited commends CPJ’s efforts to review cases and keep improving its database, when credible new information becomes available. It shows commitment to continuous improvement of their data, which increases trustworthiness.

The first phase of the review, covering 229 cases, was completed in July and its findings were presented in a confidential internal report on July 7. CPJ subsequently commissioned an external audit to assess the review’s process and findings. The findings of the review and audit were published on September 24.

Scale of journalist killings unparalleled

As a result of new information obtained through the review, CPJ removed 22 individuals previously listed as journalists or media workers from its database: newly surfaced information identified 19 individuals as combatants, while the remaining three were found to be non-journalist civilians. CPJ also reinstated six individuals and reclassified 12 cases from journalist to media worker, or vice versa. Even after these changes, the scale of journalist killings in the conflict remains unparalleled.

FPU supports CPJ’s intention to commission an external International Humanitarian Law expert to review its criteria concerning work in military media units and publish the findings. In situations of armed conflict, determining whether an individual is participating in hostilities is highly complex and directly relevant to the protections afforded to journalists as civilians under international humanitarian law.

No justice

Not a single of the 191 journalist killings has resulted in justice, despite promises of investigations. No attack on any journalist should go unpunished. Despite this impunity, journalists in Palestine continue their work resiliently. As Al Jazeera journalist Anas Al Sharif wrote in his farewell message, when he was expecting to get killed: “I have lived through pain in all its details, tasted suffering and loss many times, yet I never once hesitated to convey the truth as it is, without distortion or falsification. [...] I urge you not to let chains silence you, nor borders restrain you.”

Read the full audit by CPJ here.

item.title: Sep 22 Di, 22. Sep 2026 19:00 Uhr Machtverschiebung: Europas neue Rolle Gespräch • KörberForum
item.description:
• KörberForum
  • Europa stärken
  • Englisch
  • Gespräch
  • Europa
  • Internationale Politik
  • Internationale Verständigung

Jahrhundertelang verstand sich Europa als Zentrum der Welt. Doch mit dem Aufstieg von Ländern wie Indien, Indonesien oder Südafrika gerät dieser Anspruch ins Wanken. Der Historiker Dipesh Chakrabarty und der ehemalige Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz sprechen über Machtverschiebungen, das Ende alter Gewissheiten und über globale Gerechtigkeit.

Jahrhundertelang verstand sich Europa als Zentrum der Welt – als Maßstab, an dem sich Fortschritt, Vernunft und Ordnung bemessen ließen. Doch dieser Anspruch gerät ins Wanken. Länder wie Indien, Indonesien oder Südafrika beanspruchen Gestaltungsmacht dort, wo ihnen lange nur die Zuschauerrolle zugedacht war.

Für Europa stellt sich damit nicht nur die Frage, wie viel Gewicht es behält – sondern eine viel unbequemere: Ist es bereit, sich selbst als eine Region unter vielen zu begreifen, statt als Zentrum der Welt? Ist das ein Problem oder eher eine große Chance?

Der Historiker Dipesh Chakrabarty hat dafür einen Begriff geprägt: die Provinzialisierung Europas. Europäisches Denken sei nicht falsch, aber es ist partikular, nicht universal. Olaf Scholz hat als Bundeskanzler eine Außenpolitik der Partnerschaft auf Augenhöhe vorangetrieben. Doch müsste Europa nicht lernen, die Deutungshoheit über globale Problemlagen und Fragen selbst zur Verhandlungssache zu machen?

Wie ist die Skepsis vieler Staaten im Globalen Süden gegenüber dem Westen zu erklären? Und kann Europa weiterhin die globale Ordnung mitgestalten – und wenn ja, zu welchem Preis?

Ein Abend über Machtverschiebungen, und das Ende alter Gewissheiten und über die Frage, was Europa aufgeben müsste, damit die nächste Weltordnung eine gerechtere wird.

Es moderiert die Journalistin Xifan Yang.

Eine Veranstaltung in deutscher und englischer Sprache mit Simultanübersetzung.

Gäste

  • Dipesh Chakrabarty ist Historiker an der University of Chicago und einer der einflussreichsten Vertreter der postkolonialen Geschichtsschreibung. Sein Werk „Provincializing Europe“ gilt als Schlüsseltext der postkolonialen Theorie, das 2010 unter dem Titel „Europa als Provinz“ auf Deutsch erschien (Campus).

  • Olaf Scholz ist SPD-Abgeordneter des Deutschen Bundestages und ehemaliger Bundeskanzler der Bundesrepublik Deutschland.

Moderation

item.content:encoded:
• KörberForum
  • Europa stärken
  • Englisch
  • Gespräch
  • Europa
  • Internationale Politik
  • Internationale Verständigung

Jahrhundertelang verstand sich Europa als Zentrum der Welt. Doch mit dem Aufstieg von Ländern wie Indien, Indonesien oder Südafrika gerät dieser Anspruch ins Wanken. Der Historiker Dipesh Chakrabarty und der ehemalige Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz sprechen über Machtverschiebungen, das Ende alter Gewissheiten und über globale Gerechtigkeit.

Jahrhundertelang verstand sich Europa als Zentrum der Welt – als Maßstab, an dem sich Fortschritt, Vernunft und Ordnung bemessen ließen. Doch dieser Anspruch gerät ins Wanken. Länder wie Indien, Indonesien oder Südafrika beanspruchen Gestaltungsmacht dort, wo ihnen lange nur die Zuschauerrolle zugedacht war.

Für Europa stellt sich damit nicht nur die Frage, wie viel Gewicht es behält – sondern eine viel unbequemere: Ist es bereit, sich selbst als eine Region unter vielen zu begreifen, statt als Zentrum der Welt? Ist das ein Problem oder eher eine große Chance?

Der Historiker Dipesh Chakrabarty hat dafür einen Begriff geprägt: die Provinzialisierung Europas. Europäisches Denken sei nicht falsch, aber es ist partikular, nicht universal. Olaf Scholz hat als Bundeskanzler eine Außenpolitik der Partnerschaft auf Augenhöhe vorangetrieben. Doch müsste Europa nicht lernen, die Deutungshoheit über globale Problemlagen und Fragen selbst zur Verhandlungssache zu machen?

Wie ist die Skepsis vieler Staaten im Globalen Süden gegenüber dem Westen zu erklären? Und kann Europa weiterhin die globale Ordnung mitgestalten – und wenn ja, zu welchem Preis?

Ein Abend über Machtverschiebungen, und das Ende alter Gewissheiten und über die Frage, was Europa aufgeben müsste, damit die nächste Weltordnung eine gerechtere wird.

Es moderiert die Journalistin Xifan Yang.

Eine Veranstaltung in deutscher und englischer Sprache mit Simultanübersetzung.

Gäste

  • Dipesh Chakrabarty ist Historiker an der University of Chicago und einer der einflussreichsten Vertreter der postkolonialen Geschichtsschreibung. Sein Werk „Provincializing Europe“ gilt als Schlüsseltext der postkolonialen Theorie, das 2010 unter dem Titel „Europa als Provinz“ auf Deutsch erschien (Campus).

  • Olaf Scholz ist SPD-Abgeordneter des Deutschen Bundestages und ehemaliger Bundeskanzler der Bundesrepublik Deutschland.

Moderation

  • Xifan Yang ist Redakteurin und Reporterin in der Außenpolitikredaktion der ZEIT in Berlin. Sie berichtete von 2018 bis 2013 unter anderem als ZEIT-Korrespondentin aus Peking und 2025 aus den USA.

item.title: From surveillance to governance: recentering human rights in the UN AI agenda
item.description:
Home / Events / From surveillance to governance: recentering human rights in the UN AI agenda

September 21 @ 9:00 am – 10:30 am EDT

Hybrid side event during UNGA81 High-Level Week

In-person attendance available upon request: email [email protected]

  • Google
  • Apple
  • Outlook 365
  • Outlook Live

Panelists:

  • Louise Lund Henneberg, Acting Director/Techplomacy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Denmark
  • Wafa Ben Hassine, Chief, Digital Technology and Human Rights Section, Rule of Law, Accountability and Civic Space, Oﬀice of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
  • Beatriz Busaniche, Executive Director, Fundación Vía Libre
  • Luda Svystunova, Head of Social Research, Amundi

Moderator:

  • Alejandro Mayoral Baños, Co-Executive Director, Access Now

During the first session of the Global Dialogue on AI Governance, governments and stakeholders convened to have open, transparent and inclusive discussions on artificial intelligence governance. We now gather experts across the spectrum of stakeholders during UNGA81 to reaffirm that human rights should be the stepping stone of this process, instead of an afterthought.

None of this is irreversible, but the security issues associated with advanced AI tools are the consequences of deliberately prioritizing profit and competitiveness over the security and safety of at-risk communities, and they will not resolve on their own. Unbridled AI adoption combined with unacceptably lax corporate security practices demands urgent intervention at all levels, starting from putting human rights back at the center of digital governance mechanisms.

This discussion has the objective to explore concrete, actionable ways in which each stakeholder can contribute to oppose the normalization of surveillance. Experts will also discuss how to chart a way forward to reaffirm digital rights as the natural first line of defense against the abuses of AI technologies.

item.title: Call for quotations for the selection of a Service Provider for the organization of a two-day Podcast Forum in Bishkek
item.description:
CFI operates the Media Horizons project in Central Asia– funded by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. This regional project aims to support local initiatives for the development of the media and documentary sector in four Central Asian countries. 
Its primary goal is to strengthen the capacities of media professionals by encouraging professional exchanges, improving access to resources and expertise and supporting regional cooperation within the sector. In that aim, CFI is organizing with its partner the Bishkek Franco-German Cultural Institute a regional Podcast Forum in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on November 13th and 14th 2026. The Bishkek Podcast Forum will consist of a two-day Podcast workshop for students on 13th and 14th and a one day opened Forum on the 14th.

CFI is seeking one service provider to support the logistics and communication services of the organization of the Bishkek Podcast Forum that will take place in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan on the 13th and 14th of November 2026.

The purpose of this Call for Quotation is to define the contractual terms of the future contract, hereinafter referred to as the "contract", subsequently concluded between CFI and the selected service provider. The terms of the contract set forth in this Call for Quotation are provisional/informative and may be subject to unilateral modification by CFI prior to its conclusion.

Newsletter

The information gathered in this form is only used to send you the CFI newsletter. The information may be kept for no more than 3 years. In accordance with the Data Protection Act of 6 January 1978 amended in 2004, you have the right to access and correct information relating to you, which you can exercise via the contact form or by emailing webmaster@cfi.fr or writing to CFI, Direction générale, 62 rue Camille Desmoulins - F - 92130 Issy-les-Moulineaux.

item.title: Sep 18 Fr, 18. Sep 2026 16:00 Uhr Das Treppenhausorchester Konzert • KörberHaus
item.description:
• KörberHaus
  • Konzert
  • Gesellschaft
  • Kultur
  • Musik

Das Treppenhausorchester erobert das KörberHaus: Mit musikalischen Streifzügen durch Foyer und Etagen entsteht ein gemeinsames Klanggeschehen. Anschließend reagiert ein Streichquartett im Notfallkonzert auf kleine und große Alltagsnöte des Publikums – persönlich, überraschend und berührend.

Nachdem Mitglieder des Treppenhausorchesters musikalisch durch das Foyer und die Etagen des KörberHauses gezogen ist, lädt ein Streichquartett in den KörberSaal zu „Deinem Notfallkonzert“ ein, in dem das Streichquartett auf kleine und große Alltagsnotlagen der Gäste reagiert: Sie können Ihre persönlichen Notfälle einbringen, die dann musikalisch begleitet werden – oder einfach Teil eines berührenden Konzerterlebnisses sein.

Das Treppenhausorchester versteht sich als künstlerisches Labor für einen erweiterten Konzertbegriff. Mit spielerischem Forschungstrieb untersucht das vielfach ausgezeichnete Ensemble die Grenzen des Live-Konzerts, öffnet neue Hörerlebnisse und verbindet klassische Musik mit Performance, Raum und Lebenswirklichkeit.

Das rund 20-köpfige Orchester arbeitet regelmäßig interdisziplinär mit Künstlerinnen und Künstlern aus Regie, Film, Schauspiel und Komposition und entwickelt innovative Konzertformate wie KULT, DARK ROOM, DARK RIDE, INNER JOURNEY oder NOTFALLKONZERTE.

Es ist an renommierten Häusern und Festivals in Deutschland und Europa präsent, u.a. der Elbphilharmonie Hamburg, der Kölner Philharmonie, der Alten Oper Frankfurt und des Beethovenfests Bonn.

Die Veranstaltung ist der Auftakt mehrerer Konzerte im KörberHaus.
 

Gäste

  • Das preisgekrönte Ensemble zählt zu den führenden Vertretern der innovativen Klassikszene Europas. Es veranstaltet eigene Konzertreihen in Hannover und Hamburg und wird mit Formaten wie KULT, DARK ROOM oder DISCO regelmäßig zu internationalen Festivals eingeladen. In der treppenhauscloud bietet es seit 2025 Community-, Education- und Beteiligungsprojekte. 2021 erhielt das Treppenhausorchester den Perspektivpreis DER FAUST.

item.title: 30 Years of Stiftung Mercator: €100,000 for 30 Additional Neighbourhood Projects in the Ruhr Region
item.description:
To mark its 30th anniversary, non-profit Stiftung Mercator is providing €100,000 to Förderpott.Ruhr, a funding programme run by the Stiftungsnetzwerk Ruhr, as part of its anniversary celebration. Until 30 September 2026, 12:00 noon, individuals, non-profit organisations, initiatives and associations can apply for funding of projects that aim to improve community life in local communities across the Ruhr region. 

Förderpott.Ruhr reflects the full diversity of civic engagement across the area. Anyone committed to their community and seeking to make their neighbourhood a better place to live can receive unbureaucratic funding of between €500 and €5,000. At www.foerderpott.ruhr, applicants can describe their project idea, funding needs and the specific added value their project will bring to their district in just a few steps. 

Special Anniversary Funding from Stiftung Mercator 

In the current funding round, the initiative will be able to support significantly more applications than usual. 

“A strong civil society is essential for a vibrant democracy,” says Dr Lars Grotewold, Chief Executive Officer of Stiftung Mercator. “Especially at the local level, committed citizens who take responsibility for their neighbourhoods and initiate practical change make all the difference.” With the €100,000 in additional funding, Stiftung Mercator aims to strengthen this civic engagement. In addition to the projects selected through the regular jury process, a one-off total of 30 further projects will each receive an average of around €3,000. 

Diverse Ways of Contributing to the Common Good 

Projects funded to date across more than 80 neighbourhoods in the Ruhr region include an inclusive skateboarding project in Essen, a repair café in Duisburg, a cargo bike for an initiative in Dortmund, self-defence courses for girls in Herne, as well as projects focused on integration, democracy and social cohesion. 

Since Förderpott.Ruhr was launched in 2020, a total of 175 projects has received €538,550 in funding. This is currently the 14th round of funding of the joint initiative. The process is coordinated by Ehrenamt Agentur Essen e. V. A seven-member jury comprising representatives of funding foundations, companies and experts decides which applications receive funding. 

Förderpott.Ruhr is a joint initiative of Stiftungsnetzwerk Ruhr. Through the initiative, foundations and companies pool their resources to provide straightforward support for local civic engagement across the Ruhr region. At least €100,000 is available each year. Companies and foundations can participate with contributions starting at €1,000 per year. 

Further Information and Applications 

www.foerderpott.ruhr
 

Campaign video featuring examples of funded projects: 

YouTube – Förderpott.Ruhr campaign video 

Photos for editorial use free of charge: 

Photo selection – Förderpott.Ruhr (Dropbox) 

 

PRESS CONTACT 

Stiftung Mercator:

Lothar Kuhn | Director Communications 

T +49 201-245 22-36 | lothar.kuhn@stiftung-mercator.de 

Stiftungsnetzwerk Ruhr:

Ehrenamt Agentur Essen e. V.

T +49 201 839 149 87 | info@stiftungsnetzwerk.ruhr

 

ABOUT STIFTUNG MERCATOR 

Stiftung Mercator is a private, independent and non-profit organisation that operates on the basis of scientific expertise and practical project experience. Since 1996, it has been committed to fostering a solidary and participatory society. To this end, it supports and develops initiatives that improve opportunities for participation and strengthen social cohesion. Stiftung Mercator advocates for a capable and democratic Europe, a rights-based digital transformation of the state and society, and a resilient, socially balanced climate policy. These objectives can only be realised within a liberal democracy – one that Stiftung Mercator seeks to defend and strengthen – as expressed in its motto: #StandingUpForDemocracy.The foundation is active in Germany, across Europe, and globally. It maintains a strong connection to the Ruhr region, home to the founding family and the foundation’s headquarters. 

www.stiftung-mercator.de/en

ABOUT STIFTUNGSNETZWERK RUHR 

Stiftungsnetzwerk Ruhr (SNR) has brought together organisations from one of Germany’s most foundation-rich regions since 2016. The network currently has 96 members, ranging from local community foundations to globally active foundations based in the Ruhr region. 

Twice a year, networking meetings take place in different cities and at special locations across the Ruhr region, providing opportunities for foundations to exchange ideas, build connections and discuss current regional developments. 

The network was initiated in 2015 by Anneliese Brost-Stiftung, E.ON Foundation and Stiftung Mercator. Further supporters have joined over the years. The members E.ON Foundation, GLS Treuhand, RAG-Stiftung, Regionalverband Ruhr, Stifterverband and Wilo-Foundation form the steering committee, which oversees and finances the network. 

Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach-Stiftung and KORTE-Stiftung also provide independent funding. 

www.stiftungsnetzwerk.ruhr

T +49 201 839 149 87 | info@stiftungsnetzwerk.ruhr

 

ABOUT STIFTUNG MERCATOR 

Stiftung Mercator is a private, independent and non-profit organisation that operates on the basis of scientific expertise and practical project experience. Since 1996, it has been committed to fostering a solidary and participatory society. To this end, it supports and develops initiatives that improve opportunities for participation and strengthen social cohesion. Stiftung Mercator advocates for a capable and democratic Europe, a rights-based digital transformation of the state and society, and a resilient, socially balanced climate policy. These objectives can only be realised within a liberal democracy – one that Stiftung Mercator seeks to defend and strengthen – as expressed in its motto: #StandingUpForDemocracy.The foundation is active in Germany, across Europe, and globally. It maintains a strong connection to the Ruhr region, home to the founding family and the foundation’s headquarters. 

www.stiftung-mercator.de/en

ABOUT STIFTUNGSNETZWERK RUHR 

Stiftungsnetzwerk Ruhr (SNR) has brought together organisations from one of Germany’s most foundation-rich regions since 2016. The network currently has 96 members, ranging from local community foundations to globally active foundations based in the Ruhr region. 

Twice a year, networking meetings take place in different cities and at special locations across the Ruhr region, providing opportunities for foundations to exchange ideas, build connections and discuss current regional developments. 

The network was initiated in 2015 by Anneliese Brost-Stiftung, E.ON Foundation and Stiftung Mercator. Further supporters have joined over the years. The members E.ON Foundation, GLS Treuhand, RAG-Stiftung, Regionalverband Ruhr, Stifterverband and Wilo-Foundation form the steering committee, which oversees and finances the network. 

Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach-Stiftung and KORTE-Stiftung also provide independent funding. 

www.stiftungsnetzwerk.ruhr

item.title: Ignore human rights risks, face the consequences: Telenor under investigation for crimes against humanity in Myanmar
item.description:
Home / Press Releases / Ignore human rights risks, face the consequences: Telenor under investigation for crimes against humanity in Myanmar

On September 15, 2026, Norwegian authorities announced an investigation into Telenor for suspected crimes against humanity and sanctions violations in Myanmar following the 2021 military coup. For years, Access Now and civil society have raised the alarm over Telenor’s hasty and irresponsible departure from Myanmar and the potential human rights abuses should Telenor sell its Myanmar enterprise to the military-linked M1 Group.

The decision to file charges against Telenor follows a police complaint filed by Justice for Myanmar and ICJ Norway last year. Earlier this year, the Swedish human rights group Justice and Accountability Initiative (JAI), with the support of various Myanmar civil society organizations and EU-based groups, also filed a class-action lawsuit against Telenor.

In August 2021, Access Now, along with 44 organizations, laid out the potential dangers of this sale to the Telenor board, calling for it to stop the sale and conduct human rights due diligence in line with international standards. Telenor responded on September 3, 2021. Ultimately, Telenor refused to listen to civil society and proceeded with the sale.

Businesses have an obligation to protect and respect human rights wherever they operate and whenever they enter or leave a country, especially in conflict zones or during times of crisis. Access Now calls on companies to adhere to their human rights obligations as laid out in the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights.
